newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia court rebuffs investors in steel mill row.
newsitem.headline: Russia court rebuffs investors in steel mill row.

text.p: Bewildered investors in leading Russian steel mill Novolipetsk have lost a round in a struggle over shareholders rights but will appeal new court decisions against them, their lawyers said on Thursday.

A regional court in Lipetsk, 400 km south of Moscow, ruled against steel mill shareholders Renaissance Capital and Russia's ICFI which had protested management conduct at two previous annual meetings.
The management has refused to put up for vote a slate of directors by the outside shareholders, in a dispute watched closely as a litmus test of Russia's climate for foreign investment.

"We lost two cases," said Rafael Akopov, deputy head of legal operations for Renaissance Capital. "We haven't yet received the written decision and so we don't know how they arrived at it, but so far we are bewildered.
"We think that the legal politics of the Lipetsk court has changed towards this case in an unfortunate direction for us," Akopov said. "We will appeal, of course."
The steel mill is one of Russia's largest, producing 3.46 million tonnes of rolled steel in the first half of 1997, up six percent on the same period a year ago.
A long line of court decisions and shareholder protests have failed to sway factory management which remains in control of the plant despite the inconclusive annual meeting last month.
Shareholders failed to extend the current board's term or vote in a new board.
In May the court ordered plant management to include nominees from Renaissance, ICFI (MFK in Russian) and Cambridge Capital Management on a list of candidates to a new board of directors.
Akopov said investors still planned to call an extraordinary shareholders meeting to elect a new board of directors but were waiting for another court ruling due shortly.
"The probability of the extraordinary meeting being called before the next annual general meeting is high," said Akopov.

The three companies vowed to call a new meeting after shareholders at the AGM last month rejected a new charter allowing the current board to govern until new elections were held. No provision for elections had been made.
Renaissance Capital, MFK and Cambridge Capital Management say they together hold a controlling stake in the Novolipetsk mill. ($ = 5,805 roubles)
